# Patient RX System v2.0.67

## Security Hardening and Document Upload Removal

This release promotes the tested staging hardening work into production.

## What Changed

- Removed patient and RX document upload controls from the UI.
- Disabled patient and RX document upload API routes.
- Removed the Google Drive web-view link from document API responses.
- Stopped requesting and storing the Google Drive web-view link for new document records.
- Kept document download access role-restricted and delivered as safer attachments.
- Added login enforcement for protected HTML pages, so logged-out users are redirected to `/login`.
- Hardened System Settings email-alert user configuration rendering against stored-XSS style values.
- Added audit logging for System Settings updates with sensitive values redacted.
- Added granular email alert configuration checks per user in plain language.

## Database Impact

- No destructive schema changes.
- Existing production documents are not expected for this deployment.
- Existing patients, RX records, service-date cycles, workflow history, reports data, system settings, and audit records are preserved.
- New System Settings changes will create audit records. Passwords, secrets, tokens, and keys are redacted in those audit payloads.

## Validation Completed

- Tested on staging at `http://localhost:3100`.
- Confirmed protected pages redirect to `/login` when logged out.
- Confirmed System Settings email-alert user configuration check works after the hardening changes.
- JavaScript syntax checks passed for modified browser scripts.
- Node syntax checks passed for modified controllers/routes and `app.js`.
- Staging configuration check passed.
- A fresh production build and update zip are generated for version `2.0.67`.

## Production Verification Checklist

After installing the `v2.0.67` update:

1. Confirm the sidebar/version badge or `/api/version` shows `2.0.67`.
2. Open `/dashboard`, `/patients`, `/rx-records`, `/reports`, and `/system-settings` while logged out or in a private window. Confirm each redirects to `/login`.
3. Log in as an Administrator and open System Settings.
4. Open Email Alerts, choose a user under Check One User, and confirm the plain-language alert configuration loads.
5. Change a harmless setting such as app name or timezone, then open Audit Log and confirm a `System Settings` / `Settings Updated` entry exists.
6. Open a patient and RX record and confirm there is no document upload option.
7. If any old document records exist, confirm downloads still require the proper role and no Google Drive web-view link is shown in the UI.
